intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the CFAP47 gene (301057) on chromosome Xp21.1.

checks.claim: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is caused by hemizygous mutation in the CFAP47 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: our experimental observations in humans and mice demonstrate that hemizygous mutations in CFAP47 can induce X-linked MMAF and asthenoteratozoospermia
checks.explanation: The paper does not use the SPGFX3 label, but the X-linked disorder it describes is the same one.

checks.claim: The CFAP47 gene is located on chromosome Xp21.1.
checks.evidence_quote: permitted the identification of a hemizygous Xp21.1 deletion removing the entire CFAP47 gene
checks.explanation: The deletion at Xp21.1 removes the whole CFAP47 gene, so the gene lies at Xp21.1.

paragraphs.text: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is a form of primary male infertility. It is characterized by asthenoteratozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF) (Liu et al., 2021).

checks.claim: X-linked spermatogenic failure-3 (SPGFX3) is a form of primary male infertility.
checks.evidence_quote: Deleterious variants in X-linked CFAP47 induce asthenoteratozoospermia and primary male infertility.
checks.explanation: The title states that the condition is primary male infertility.

checks.claim: SPGFX3 is characterized by asthenoteratozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF).
checks.evidence_quote: Asthenoteratozoospermia characterized by multiple morphological abnormalities of the flagella (MMAF) has been identified as a sub-type of male infertility.
checks.explanation: The paper describes the phenotype as asthenoteratozoospermia with MMAF.

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2021) reported 3 unrelated Chinese men with primary infertility caused by asthenoteratozoospermia with multiple morphological abnormalities of the sperm flagella (MMAF). Immunoblotting and immunofluorescence showed obviously reduced levels of CFAP47 in spermatozoa from all 3 men. Liu et al. (2021) also reported an Australian man from a cohort of men with severe asthenoteratozoospermia. According to the authors, all of the men with hemizygous CFAP47 variants had typical MMAF phenotypes.

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2021) identified hemizygous missense mutations in the X-linked CFAP47 gene in 3 unrelated Chinese men with MMAF. The 3 variants were absent from human control population genome databases. Multiple bioinformatic tools predicted them to be deleterious. Spermatozoa from all 3 men had obviously reduced levels of CFAP47 on immunoblotting and immunofluorescence. CFAP47 encodes a cilia- and flagella-associated protein that is highly expressed in testis.

paragraphs.text: Liao et al. (2022) screened 7 men with MMAF for mutations. In 1 of them they found 2 novel CFAP47 mutations: a c.706G-A change resulting in a val236-to-met (V236M) substitution, and a c.1337C-T change resulting in a thr446-to-met (T446M) substitution. CFAP47 was dramatically reduced in this man's spermatozoa on immunoblotting and immunofluorescence.

paragraphs.text: Liao et al. (2022) found that CFAP47 interacted with WDR87 in the midpiece of the sperm flagellum. They suggested that the 2 proteins form a complex involved in sperm tail assembly. In sperm from a man with CFAP47 mutations, WDR87 expression was markedly reduced, with weak signals next to the sperm nuclei. The authors concluded that CFAP47 is needed to transport WDR87 during flagellar biogenesis.
